Hi everyone! I’m Emanuele Di Bella, and I’m about to conclude my PhD in Mathematics, specializing in computational algebra.

My research focuses on Lie algebras, nilpotent orbits, and exact algorithmic computation. I have mainly written advanced algorithms in Magma and GAP. I also have strong background in other ares of algebra (like group theory)

I have been following the explosion of Lean 4 and the growth of Mathlib with huge interest recentely. I am completely new to Lean, but I am used to strict formal logic and exact computation, so I’m eager to learn.

I have two quick questions for the community:

What is the current status of Lie Theory/Group Theory in Mathlib? I would love to start translating some of my algebraic knowledge into Lean code.

Career-wise: I am actively looking for Postdoc, RSE, or similar positions in Europe. Does anyone know of research groups or PIs who are currently hiring mathematicians with a strong computational algebra background who are willing to transition into Lean/formalization?

Welcome!

Emanuele Di Bella said:

What is the current status of Lie Theory/Group Theory in Mathlib?

Do the mathlib overview / undergrad overview help? What are you looking for exactly? Perhaps you could name‑drop some concepts/theorems that you're wondering whether mathlib has?

What is the current status of Lie Theory/Group Theory in Mathlib? I would love to start translating some of my algebraic knowledge into Lean code.

There is some material here: Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold. The Lie exponential map does not yet exist which I need and here are some of my thoughts on proving it using a theorem in Lee's book: https://github.com/idontgetoutmuch/mathlib4/blob/smooth-exp-Lie-V/Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/Algebra/SmoothLieExp.lean (well amongst other things).
